name: Rose Keep — surface and detail kit
prompt:
Create ONE labelled GAME ASSET COMPONENT SKETCH SHEET titled B04-DETAIL-001 — ROSE KEEP FITTINGS. Use ONLY the attached original Rose Keep image as style reference: blush-pink limestone, pale cream carved stone, restrained muted-gold accents, burgundy shingle cones, delicate arched windows and climbing-rose motifs. Keep this modest rose keep distinct from the huge princess palace. Fine crisp stone carving and readable physical thickness, precise clean hard-surface forms, no melted or distorted decor. Neutral ivory studio background, even light, wide landscape composition, generous spacing.

EXACTLY TWELVE independent cells arranged 4 columns by 3 rows, one isolated complete component per cell, clear three-quarter view showing depth. Each cell is independently scaled for readability, NOT a common object scale. Exact short ID D01 through D12 and name beneath each, title establishes the full B04-DETAIL-001 prefix. Separate objects, no touching, no environment scene and no complete building. Every decorated object needs its visible mounting face or profile. Dimensions below are proposed construction, not measured source facts. Use fine simple labels; no labels across geometry.

ROW 1:
D01 BURGUNDY CONE QUADRANT. One 90-degree quarter-shell of a tall pointed conical roof, base radius 6.2 m, height 12 m, thin hollow underside, crisp matched radial seam edges. Burgundy tiny regular shingle pattern, restrained pale eave seat. One quadrant only; four rotated copies would make a 12.4 m diameter roof for a 12 m outside-diameter turret. Show the curved outside and one exposed cut edge so the hollow conical shell is clear. NOT an onion dome, not a complete cone and not a tall tower.
D02 CURVED TURRET CORNICE. One pale-stone 30-degree circular cornice segment for a 6 m radius turret; simple moulded stepped profile, both radial joining ends visible. Twelve matching segments would form a ring. Restrained shallow rose/leaf detail, no column below it or whole ring. Section depth about 0.35 m and vertical height 0.45 m; hidden attachment construction inferred.
D03 ARCHED WINDOW INSERT. One slim pointed-arch frame and subtle quiet glass pane, nominal width 1.78 m and height 5.98 m, thickness 0.12 m. Tall simple jambs, shallow tracery, pale stone and tiny muted-gold fittings. It fits a 1.8 m wide / 6 m high turret opening with slight clearance. No enclosing wall, huge starburst or saturated blue-pink palace window.
D04 ROSE WALL RELIEF. One small shallow stone rose-and-leaf carving, 0.45 m wide, about 0.04 m relief, flat mounting back. Single readable carved flower, no growing bush or whole wall plaque.

ROW 2:
D05 PARAPET REPEAT. One 1 m long, 1.1 m tall, 0.12 m nominal-deep guard repeat, pale stone and modest carved openings consistent with the source's terrace edges; constant planar matching end joins, clean base mounting strip. Crisp intact form, no wall/building below it. Height is a proposed drop-guard adaptation; do not imply the thumbnail provides measured balusters.
D06 PARAPET CORNER CAP. One small matching 90-degree corner connector with two perpendicular short ends, same pale stone section language and top moulding as D05; about 0.35 m by 0.35 m footprint and 1.1 m high. Show the real L section in oblique view, not a new unrelated tower.
D07 EMPTY ARCH SURROUND. One separate pointed-arch pale stone band; EMPTY centre all the way through. Clear inner width 2.4 m, vertical-jamb spring 3.2 m, apex 3.8 m; outside width 3.2 m, outside height 4.3 m, flat back, 0.2 m projection. Restrained rose/leaf corner carving only. No gate leaf, infill or building wall attached.
D08 STAIR RAIL RETURN. One matching pale stone handrail/edge return, about 1 m developed length, 0.12 m section depth, with a gently rounded turn at the end and slim supports below it; handrail about 1.1 m above its support datum. Clearly a small rail transition, not a staircase or whole balustraded terrace. Curved section should be clean and non-self-intersecting.

ROW 3:
D09 FLAT ROSE FLOOR TILE. One square 1.5 m by 1.5 m, 0.12 m thick tile, TOP surface up. Shallow blush/cream geometric border and small rose-inlay rhythm, no raised flower sculpture. Straight complementary repeat edges; reveal a thin side so it reads as flooring. This interior-facing pattern is inferred from local materials, not directly visible in the source.
D10 IVORY WALL DADO. One plain-backed wall-mountable 1 m long, 0.65 m high, 0.08 m thick lower wall panel, cream stone with quiet blush inset and restrained horizontal moulding. Flat rear and straight joining ends. Decorated main face vertical, not floor tile or thick box. Proposed local interior adaptation.
D11 CEILING BEAM BRACKET. One small 0.3 m wide, 0.5 m deep, 0.6 m high supporting corbel, pale stone with a simple rose-leaf profile, flat wall back and flat horizontal beam seat. It must visibly support something above, not be a loose ornate capital. Proposed hidden-face construction.
D12 TRELLIS HOOK. One small muted-gold or aged brass wall hook, 0.2 m wide, 0.12 m projection, 0.25 m high, flat two-hole mounting plate and a curved trellis tie hook. One complete attached hardware item only. No rose vine, trellis panel, lantern, complete arch or scenery fused to it.

Every part has distinct solid, readable structure, restrained fine ornament and a clear mounting/connection face. No competing unrelated new motifs, no giant lotus capitals, no indigo star collars, no purple onion roofs, no palace redesign, people, scenery, tangled flowers or watermark. Footer: PROPOSED LOCAL FITTINGS • source motifs preserved, hidden construction inferred • physical joins and model topology unverified. These are design references, not accepted final 3D models.
